failures.criterion: INFRA-514 architect's check (dispatch://INFRA-593/comment/542d490a-194e-4c90-9cf2-243ecc788b28): the hourly compaction sweep, when nothing is due, does an index read of due documents only, no scan of every document.
failures.evidence: compactionCandidates (internal/dispatch/docs/compaction_sweep.go:133-143) runs `select artifact_id from doc_updates group by artifact_id having count(*) > 1` every hour. EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) on 100,000 one-row documents, none due: HashAggregate over Seq Scan on doc_updates, Rows Removed by Filter: 100000, shared hit=11334 (the whole 89 MB heap), 113 ms; with compressible 2-KB rows also a Seq Scan, 77 ms. The PR body's 2,000,000-row run got an index-only scan of the primary key; either plan reads one entry per document. Plan D3 chose this query and forbids a doc_updates migration, so the remedy is the architect's decision. Red test (commit 267322ef): TestTheCompactionSweepReadsNoRowOfADocumentThatIsNotDue in packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/docs/compaction_sweep_test.go; `cd packages/envoy && DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL=<postgres> go test ./internal/dispatch/docs -run TestTheCompactionSweepReadsNoRowOfADocumentThatIsNotDue -count=3` fails 3 of 3: 'the sweep read 2024 doc_updates rows to fold one document of 3 rows among 2000 documents with nothing to fold, want fewer than 2000'. The due document's own reads are 21 rows, so a listing of due documents only passes.
